label: Perimeter & Circumference
overview: Perimeter is the total distance around a 2D figure, found by summing all side lengths. Circumference is the perimeter of a circle. SAT questions combine perimeter with area, ask for missing sides given a perimeter, or embed perimeter in word problems about fencing, framing, or wrapping.

workedExamples.problem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 cm and a width of 8 cm. What is the length?

steps.title: Use the perimeter formula
steps.content: Set up the equation with P = 46 and w = 8.

workedExamples.problem: A circle has a circumference of 20π. What is the diameter?

steps.title: Use C = πd
steps.content: Set πd = 20π and divide both sides by π.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mixing up perimeter (add sides) and area (space inside)
commonMistakes.fix: Perimeter is a length (units like cm). Area is square units (cm²). Make sure the question is asking for one-dimensional boundary, not two-dimensional space.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using radius when the formula needs diameter (or vice versa)
commonMistakes.fix: C = 2πr = πd. If given radius r, multiply by 2 to get diameter d.

quickTip: For any polygon (not just standard shapes), perimeter is always just the sum of all side lengths — no special formula needed.
